PUBLIC RESPONSE: The asymptotic $f^{k}\to0$ calculation is formally correct for a fixed set of frequencies, but it does not match how the data are actually generated here.

The VCF union is fixed by the pre-filtering ascertainment, but the filtering is per-haplotype and random. After filtering and reference imputation a true derived copy is present in the imputed sequence iff the call is retained in that haplotype. Imputation can only turn a true derived allele into reference, never the reverse. Hence the imputed allele count at a site is a thinned version of the true count.

For a site with true derived copies $k\ge1$,

$\Pr[\text{site is observed as segregating}\mid k]=1-f^{k}$

where $f$ is the per-haplotype loss probability. That is $<1$ for all finite $k$. A site is therefore lost from $S_{obs}$ whenever all $k$ carriers happen to be among the filtered calls for that site. Under the infinite-sites model the site frequency spectrum is $ \propto 1/k$, so the number of sites with bounded $k$ grows with the panel. The expected number of segregating sites lost is

$\sum_{k\ge1} N_k f^{k} =\text{const}>0$,

with $-\log(1-f)$ the $k$-sum in expectation. The $O(1)$ loss is negligible against $a_n\sim\log n$ only in the strict $n\to\infty$ mathematical limit. For any realisable, arbitrarily large but finite panel the loss is real and it is concentrated on rare variants, which dominate both $S$ and $\pi$. In practice the guarantee “no SNV is completely missing across all samples” is a pre-filtering property of the VCF. After sample-specific deletion and reference imputation a site can be rendered monomorphic reference in the imputed haplotypes if the few carriers are exactly the ones deleted in those haplotypes. That is a systematic downward bias in the segregating site count.

That same thinning deflates allele frequencies: $E[\hat p]=(1-f)p$, so $E[\hat\pi]=2(1-f)p[1-(1-f)p]<2p(1-p)$. The pairwise difference is therefore systematically under-estimated at every site, and the bias persists in the $n\to\infty$ limit.

So the reference imputation removes variation in two ways: it can erase entire segregating sites, especially rare ones, thereby depressing $S$ and Watterson’s $\theta_W=S/a_n$, and it attenuates the allele frequencies that enter $\pi$. The $\pi$ bias is larger in magnitude and asymptotically non-vanishing, but $\theta_W$ is also downward biased for any finite panel, and the bias is not qualitatively different from the one affecting $\pi$. Describing the method as “Watterson unbiased, $\pi$ biased” hides the fact that the $O(1/\log n)$ site loss is a real, systematic reference bias in the data we actually compute with. Both estimators are downward biased by the random deletion + reference imputation.

On a true site with derived copy number $i\ge 1$ in $2n$ haplotypes the observed copy number after independent thinning is $Y|i\sim {\rm Bin}(i,1-f)$. Imputation to reference sets $H_{ij}=T_{ij}$ if retained and $H_{ij}=0$ otherwise, so the observed derived frequency is $E[\hat p|p]=(1-f)p$.

Segregation. A true segregating site is lost from the observed set iff $Y=0$
$$
\Pr[Y=0|i]=f^{\,i}.
$$
With the infinite-sites spectrum $P[I=i]\propto i^{-1}$,
$$
E[S_{\rm obs}]=E[S_{\rm true}]-\sum_{i\ge1}\frac{f^{\,i}}{i}
 =E[S_{\rm true}]+\log(1-f),
$$
so the absolute loss $-\log(1-f)<\infty$ is $O(1)$ whereas $E[S_{\rm true}]=\theta a_{n}\sim\theta\log n\to\infty$.  For any fixed $p>0$, $i=2np\to\infty$ and $f^{\,i}\to0$. With the stated guarantee that no SNV is completely absent from the cohort after filtering the site stays segregating w.p.1 in the large $n$ limit, $S_{\rm obs}=S_{\rm true}$ on the ascertained union $V$, and

$$
\hat\theta_{W}^{\rm obs}=S_{\rm obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow{p}\theta_{W}^{\rm true}.
$$

Imputation to reference can never create a new segregating site, and the probability of losing the last derived copy vanishes with $n$. Up to the usual $O(1/\log n)$ finite-$n$ singleton loss, Watterson’s presence/absence statistic is preserved.

Pairwise diversity. For a site with true derived frequency $p$
$$
E\big[\hat p\big]=(1-f)p,
\qquad 
E\big[2\hat p(1-\hat p)\mid p\big]=2(1-f)p\bigl[1-(1-f)p\bigr]
      =(1-f)2p(1-p)+O(p^{2})<2p(1-p),
$$
so the expected observed pairwise difference is a constant factor deflated by the $1-f$ thinning. Hence
$$
E[\pi_{\rm obs}]=(1-f)\pi_{\rm true}+o(1),
$$
in the rare-variant limit $E[\pi_{\rm obs}]\approx(1-f)\pi_{\rm true}$. Reference imputation systematically turns filtered derived alleles into reference alleles, removing real mismatches. The bias persists for every $p>0$ and does not vanish as $n\to\infty$.

Thus on the ascertained variable-site panel Watterson’s $\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically unbiased while nucleotide diversity $\pi$ remains systematically downward biased by the random reference imputation. The finite-$n$ $O(1/\log n)$ loss of very rare sites is negligible in the arbitrarily large-sample regime stated.

11.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. Only pi (nucleotide diversity) is biased in the large-sample limit while Watterson’s θW on the ascertained VCF set is asymptotically preserved.

Let f be the per-haplotype per-site filtering probability, 0<f<1, and let the true derived copy number at a site be k ≥1 in 2n haplotypes, p=k/2n. After independent filtering

Y|k ∼ Bin(k,1-f) ,   P[Y=0|k]=f^{k}.

A site is scored as segregating after reference imputation iff Y>0. Hence

E[Sobs]=∑sites[1- f^{k}] ,   E[Strue]=∑sites 1 .

With the infinite-sites neutral spectrum E[# sites with k copies]∝1/k,

∑sites f^{k}=∑_{k≥1}c/k f^{k}=c[-log(1-f)]<∞

while E[Strue]=c a_{2n} with a_{2n}=∑_{i≤2n}1/i∼log n→∞. Thus

E[Sobs]/E[Strue]=1- [-log(1-f)]/a_{2n}→1  as n→∞

and for any fixed p>0 f^{k}=f^{2np}→0. With the stated no-complete-missing-SNV ascertainment the VCF union V is fixed and

Pr[ site in V is lost | p>0]=f^{k}→0 ,  Sobs→Stue w.p.1.

Imputation to reference can only turn a derived allele into reference, it can never create a new segregating site. Hence on the ascertained set

θ̂Wobs=Sobs/a_n → Strue/a_n =θWtrue,

up to a vanishing O(1/log n) loss of the very rare singletons. Frequency independent presence/absence is essentially preserved.

Allele frequency is not preserved. Conditional on true frequency p,

E[ p̂ | p]=(1-f)p ,   E[2p̂(1-p̂)|p]=2(1-f)p[1-(1-f)p] <2p(1-p).

Hence

E[πobs]=∑sites 2(1-f)p[1-(1-f)p] < ∑sites2p(1-p)=πtrue,

and for rare variants E[πobs]/πtrue→1-f. The thinning of derived copies by the filter and the systematic replacement of the filtered copies by the reference allele removes heterozygosity in a frequency dependent way. The bias is a constant factor 1-f and does not vanish with n. In the usual rare-variant limit πobs≈(1-f)πtrue.

That is the familiar robustness of Watterson’s segregating-site count to random, reference-imputed missingness versus the systematic downward attenuation of nucleotide diversity. Strictly finite n Watterson is O(1/log n) down, but in the arbitrarily large-sample limit the only systematic bias that remains is the downward bias of π.

9.text:
The VCF union $V$ is the ascertained set of sites that are segregating in the
panel. Let $f>0$ be the per-haplotype deletion probability and
$1-f$ the retention probability.  For a true site with $k\ge 1$ derived
copies in $2n$ haplotypes the observed copy number after the random
quality filter is $K\sim {\rm Bin}(k,1-f)$ and the imputed haplotype is
$H_{ij}=T_{ij}$ if retained and $H_{ij}=0$ ref if deleted.

*Segregating sites.* A true segregating site is lost from the imputed
data iff $K=0$,

${\mathbb P}\{K=0\mid k\}=f^{\,k}$ .

Hence

${\mathbb E}[S_{obs}\mid S_{true}]
= \sum_{sites}\bigl[1-f^{\,k}\bigr]
= S_{true}-\sum_{sites}f^{\,k}$ .

$\sum_{k\ge1}f^{k}/k=-\log(1-f)<\infty$, so the absolute loss of
segregating sites is $O(1)$.  With Watterson

$\hat\theta_{W}=S_{obs}/a_{n},\qquad a_{n}=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}1/i\sim\log n,$

${\mathbb E}[\hat\theta_{W}]/\theta_{W}^{\rm true}
 =1-\frac{-\log(1-f)}{a_{n}}+o(a_{n}^{-1})\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.$

For any fixed $p>0$, $k=2np\to\infty$ and $f^{k}\to0$, so
${\mathbb P}\{K>0\mid p>0\}\to1$.  With the stated no-completely-missing-SNV
condition the set of sites that can be examined is essentially preserved by
reference imputation. The presence/absence information on which $S$ and
hence $\theta_{W}$ is based is asymptotically unchanged; the $O(1)$ loss of
rare singletons is negligible against the $a_{n}\sim\log n$ normalisation in
the arbitrarily large-sample limit.

*Pairwise diversity.* Conditional on a true derived frequency $p$,

${\mathbb E}[\hat p\mid p]=(1-f)p$,

and

${\mathbb E}\bigl[2\hat p(1-\hat p)\mid p\bigr]
 =2(1-f)p\bigl[1-(1-f)p\bigr]
 <2p(1-p)$ .

The thinning $p\to(1-f)p$ and the replacement of deleted derived copies by
the reference allele systematically erase pairwise differences. In the
rare-variant limit the deflation is $1-f$,

${\mathbb E}[\pi_{obs}\mid p]\approx(1-f)\,\pi_{true}$,

and the bias persists for every $n$, $f>0$. Reference imputation therefore
deflates heterozygosity and nucleotide diversity by a constant factor.

Hence on the ascertained VCF set Watterson’s $S/a_{n}$ is asymptotically
preserved in the large-$n$ limit while the frequency weighted $\pi$ remains
systematically downward biased by the $(1-f)$ thinning.  In practice the
finite-$n$ absolute loss $S_{obs}<S_{true}$ gives a vanishing
$O(1/\log n)$ downward bias to $\theta_{W}$, the practically relevant
persistent bias is that of $\pi$.

B. Only pi (nucleotide diversity) is biased, $\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically
unbiased on the ascertained set in the arbitrarily large-sample limit.

$$

PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. Only pi (nucleotide diversity) is biased by the random reference imputation, Watterson’s θ is asymptotically preserved on the ascertained SNV set.

Let $r=1-f$ be the per-haplotype retention probability and $k\ge1$ the true number of derived copies at a site in $2n$ haplotypes, $p=k/2n$. After independent thinning and reference imputation

$Y_{ij}=X_{ij}{\bf1}_{\rm retained}$,  $E[Y_{ij}\mid X_{ij}=1]=r$,
$E[\hat p\mid p]=rp$,

so that for the site

$E[2\hat p(1-\hat p)\mid p]=2rp\,[1-rp]<2p(1-p)$.

The observed pairwise difference is therefore deflated by the constant factor $r$ and the missing derived alleles are systematically replaced by reference. In particular
$E[\hat\pi_{obs}]= \sum_s 2r p_s[1-rp_s]<\sum_s2p_s(1-p_s)=\pi_{true}$
and the bias persists for every $p>0$ and does not vanish with $n$. This is the usual reference-imputation downward bias of heterozygosity.

Segregation is a $0/1$ property. A truly segregating site is lost after imputation iff all $k$ derived copies are filtered out,

$P\{{\rm lost}\mid k\}=f^{\,k}$,

so that

$E[S_{obs}]= \sum_{sites}\bigl[1-f^{k}\bigr]
      =E[S_{true}]-\sum_{sites}f^{k}$.

Under the infinite-sites neutral spectrum $\sum_{sites}f^{k}= \sum_{i\ge1}f^{i}/i=-\log(1-f)=O(1)$ whereas
$E[S_{true}]=\theta a_{2n}$ with $a_{2n}\sim\log n\to\infty$.
Hence

$\frac{E[S_{obs}]}{E[S_{true}]}=1-\frac{-\log(1-f)}{a_{2n}}\to1$
and for any fixed $p>0$, $k=O(n)$ and $f^{k}\to0$.
With the stated “no completely missing SNV across the cohort’’ condition the site is never lost completely and in the $n\to\infty$ limit

$P\{S_{obs}=S_{true}\}\to1$,
$\hat\theta_{W}^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow{p}\hat\theta_{W}^{true}$.

The presence/absence information on which Watterson’s estimator is based is therefore asymptotically preserved by random reference imputation, up to the vanishing $O(1/\log n)$ loss of the rarest variants. The frequency-weighted $\pi$ is not rescued.

On the ascertained variant set $V$ the number-of-sites statistic is essentially unbiased in the arbitrarily large-sample limit, the only non-vanishing systematic bias induced by the filter+reference imputation is the downward bias of nucleotide diversity. The $O(1/\log n)$ finite-$n$ loss of $S$ is the finite-sample artefact that gives rise to the “both biased’’ comment, but it disappears relatively as $n\to\infty$.

14.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the consensus that nucleotide diversity is systematically deflated by reference imputation and that this bias does not vanish with sample size. That part is essentially undisputed: a true derived allele is seen only with probability 1-f, so E[ p̂ ] = (1-f)p and E[π̂_i]=2(1-f)p[1-(1-f)p] <2p(1-p) for every site. The imputation replaces deleted derived copies by the ancestral allele, so pairwise differences are removed in expectation.

The same imputation also changes the segregating-site count that goes into Watterson. A site is counted by θ_W = S/a_n only if at least one observed derived copy survives the per-haplotype quality filter and the subsequent reference imputation. With per-haplotype loss probability f>0 and true derived copy number k_i ≥1,

Pr[ site i is observed as segregating | k_i ] = 1 - f^{k_i} < 1

and the site can be turned into apparent monomorphic reference only, never created. Hence

E[ S_obs ] = Σ_i [1 - f^{k_i}] < Σ_i 1 = S_true

for any fixed f>0. The condition “no completely missing SNV across all samples” is a pre-filtering ascertainment condition on the raw VCF; after the independent per-sample deletions the few remaining derived copies of a low-frequency site can all be the ones that are filtered out in those samples. The site is then scored as monomorphic reference in the imputed haplotypes and is lost from S.

The infinite-sites spectrum is dominated by rare variants. The expected absolute loss Σ_i f^{k_i} = Σ_i f^{i}/i = -log(1-f) >0 is O(1) per unit θ, i.e. a non-vanishing number of singletons and low-frequency sites are removed in expectation. The loss is O(1/log n) relative to a_n, which is why the ratio E[S_obs]/E[S_true] →1 in the mathematical n→∞ limit, but the expectation inequality E[S_obs] < S_true holds for every finite, albeit arbitrarily large, panel. In practice the per-sample filter removes a substantial minority of calls, so the observed set of segregating sites is a proper downward-biased subset of the true segregating set.

Therefore the frequency-independent count S that underlies θ_W is attenuated by the same reference imputation that attenuates allele frequencies, and the frequency-weighted π is attenuated as well. Both θ_W and π are systematically downward biased by random per-sample filtering followed by reference imputation, the bias in π persisting as a constant factor and the bias in θ_W persisting as a non-zero absolute loss of rare segregating sites. That is the usual “both are deflated by missing-as-reference” behaviour.

The asymptotic argument for Watterson is a limit result and it is being overstated for the set-up we actually have.

Let f>0 be the per-haplotype filtering probability and let a site have i≥1 true derived copies in the 2n haplotypes. After independent filtering the number of observed derived copies is Bin(i,1-f) and the site is scored as monomorphic after reference imputation iff all i copies are lost. 

Pr[site lost | i] = f^{i}
E[S_obs | S_true] = Σ_{sites} [1 - f^{i}] = S_true - Σ_{sites} f^{i}.

Under the infinite-sites frequency spectrum the number of sites with i copies is proportional to 1/i. Hence the expected absolute number of sites lost is

 Σ_{i≥1} f^{i}/i = -log(1-f) >0

for every f>0. That is a finite positive loss, not a disappearing one. The relative loss is

E[S_obs]/E[S_true] = 1 - [-log(1-f)] / a_{2n}

so the fraction lost goes to zero like 1/log n, but the absolute expected loss stays >0 for every realizable panel. With a “substantial minority” filtered per sample f is not tiny, and the panel is arbitrarily large but finite. In any finite n the singleton loss alone gives a downward bias in S and therefore in θW = S/a_n. The statement that f^{i}→0 for fixed i as n→∞ is true, but i is not fixed in the infinite-sites spectrum: there is an unbounded tail of sites with i = O(1) while n grows, and those are precisely the sites that dominate the loss term Σ f^{i}/i. That is the O(1/log n) downward bias noted above, and it is systematic, not random.

π is also systematically deflated. Conditional on a true derived frequency p, the observed frequency is E[ p̂ | p ] = (1-f)p and

E[ 2p̂(1-p̂) | p ] = 2(1-f)p [1-(1-f)p] < 2p(1-p),

so reference imputation erases a fraction f of derived copies in expectation and the bias persists in the n→∞ limit. The thinning survives because allele frequencies are frequency dependent.

Hence on the ascertained variant set the counting statistic is attenuated by the non-zero probability that all carriers of a rare site are filtered in their own haplotypes, and the heterozygosity statistic is attenuated by the (1-f) thinning of derived alleles. Both S/a_n and the average pairwise difference are therefore downward biased in any finite, arbitrarily large but realizable panel, with the Watterson bias vanishing only in the mathematical n→∞ limit while the π bias does not. In practice we get a systematic downward bias in both estimators under random per-sample filtering followed by reference imputation.

The observed data are the union $V$ of SNVs that survive in at least one haplotype after
per-haplotype random thinning with retention $r=1-f<1$ and reference imputation
$H_{ij}=T_{ij}$ if retained and $H_{ij}=0$ if filtered.

For a true site with $k\ge1$ derived copies in $2n$ haplotypes the number of
derived copies that survive is $K\sim{\rm Bin}(k,r)$ and

${\rm Pr}\{K=0\mid k\}=f^{\,k}$ .

The site is scored as segregating after imputation iff $K>0$. With the stated
no-complete-missing-site condition a site in $V$ is by construction observed
as segregating in at least one sample. For a fixed $p>0$, $k=2np\to\infty$ with
$n\to\infty$ and $f^{k}\to0$. Hence

${\rm Pr}\{\hbox{site lost}\mid p>0\}=f^{k}\to0$,

and

$\displaystyle 
E[S_{obs}] =\sum_{s\in V}\Big[1-f^{k_{s}}\Big]
          =|V|-\sum_{s}f^{k_{s}}$.
$\sum_{s}f^{k_{s}}=O(1)$ whereas $E[S_{true}]=|V|$ grows like
$\theta a_{n}$ with $a_{n}=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}1/i\sim\log n\to\infty$.
Thus $E[S_{obs}]/E[S_{true}]\to1$ and in the $n\to\infty$ limit
$S_{obs}=S_{true}$ w.p.1 on the ascertained set $V$. Reference imputation can
only turn derived $\to$ reference, it never creates a new segregating site,
so the presence/absence information on which

$\hat\theta_{W}=S_{obs}/a_{n}$

is based is preserved. Up to the $O\!\left(-\log(1-f)/a_{n}\right)$ loss of
extreme singletons, $\hat\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically unbiased for the
ascertained variant set $V$, i.e. essentially the same as it would be on the
true genotypes.

Pairwise diversity is frequency dependent. Conditional on true derived
frequency $p$,

$E[\hat p\mid p]=r p$,

and for two independent haplotypes

$E\!\left[|O_{1}-O_{2}|\mid p\right]=2rp\bigl[1-rp\bigr]
      <2p(1-p)$,

with strict inequality for every $0<r<1,\;0<p<1$. Hence

$E[\pi_{obs}\mid p]=2rp\bigl[1-rp\bigr]
      =(1-f)\,2p(1-p)+O(p^{2})<2p(1-p)$,

and in the rare-variant limit $E[\pi_{obs}]\approx r\,\pi_{true}$.
Missing alternative alleles are replaced by the reference allele, so the
observed allele frequency is attenuated by the constant factor $r$ and
pairwise differences are systematically under-estimated. The deflation
persists for every $p>0$ and does not vanish as $n\to\infty$.

Hence on the ascertained SNV set $V$ Watterson’s $S/a_{n}$ is asymptotically
preserved by random reference imputation whereas nucleotide diversity stays
systematically downward biased. The usual $r$ attenuation of $\pi$ is the
dominant bias induced by filtering + reference imputation; the
$O(1/\log n)$ loss of $S$ vanishes in the arbitrarily large-sample limit
stated.

This is the conventional robustness of $\theta_{W}$ to random missingness
versus the non-robustness of $\pi$.  B.

The asymptotic $f^{k}\to0$ calculation is formally correct for a fixed set of frequencies, but it does not match how the data are actually generated here.

The VCF union is fixed by the pre-filtering ascertainment, but the filtering is per-haplotype and random. After filtering and reference imputation a true derived copy is present in the imputed sequence iff the call is retained in that haplotype. Imputation can only turn a true derived allele into reference, never the reverse. Hence the imputed allele count at a site is a thinned version of the true count.

For a site with true derived copies $k\ge1$,

$\Pr[\text{site is observed as segregating}\mid k]=1-f^{k}$

where $f$ is the per-haplotype loss probability. That is $<1$ for all finite $k$. A site is therefore lost from $S_{obs}$ whenever all $k$ carriers happen to be among the filtered calls for that site. Under the infinite-sites model the site frequency spectrum is $ \propto 1/k$, so the number of sites with bounded $k$ grows with the panel. The expected number of segregating sites lost is

$\sum_{k\ge1} N_k f^{k} =\text{const}>0$,

with $-\log(1-f)$ the $k$-sum in expectation. The $O(1)$ loss is negligible against $a_n\sim\log n$ only in the strict $n\to\infty$ mathematical limit. For any realisable, arbitrarily large but finite panel the loss is real and it is concentrated on rare variants, which dominate both $S$ and $\pi$. In practice the guarantee “no SNV is completely missing across all samples” is a pre-filtering property of the VCF. After sample-specific deletion and reference imputation a site can be rendered monomorphic reference in the imputed haplotypes if the few carriers are exactly the ones deleted in those haplotypes. That is a systematic downward bias in the segregating site count.

That same thinning deflates allele frequencies: $E[\hat p]=(1-f)p$, so $E[\hat\pi]=2(1-f)p[1-(1-f)p]<2p(1-p)$. The pairwise difference is therefore systematically under-estimated at every site, and the bias persists in the $n\to\infty$ limit.

So the reference imputation removes variation in two ways: it can erase entire segregating sites, especially rare ones, thereby depressing $S$ and Watterson’s $\theta_W=S/a_n$, and it attenuates the allele frequencies that enter $\pi$. The $\pi$ bias is larger in magnitude and asymptotically non-vanishing, but $\theta_W$ is also downward biased for any finite panel, and the bias is not qualitatively different from the one affecting $\pi$. Describing the method as “Watterson unbiased, $\pi$ biased” hides the fact that the $O(1/\log n)$ site loss is a real, systematic reference bias in the data we actually compute with. Both estimators are downward biased by the random deletion + reference imputation.

I agree with the consensus that nucleotide diversity is systematically deflated by reference imputation and that this bias does not vanish with sample size. That part is essentially undisputed: a true derived allele is seen only with probability 1-f, so E[ p̂ ] = (1-f)p and E[π̂_i]=2(1-f)p[1-(1-f)p] <2p(1-p) for every site. The imputation replaces deleted derived copies by the ancestral allele, so pairwise differences are removed in expectation.

The same imputation also changes the segregating-site count that goes into Watterson. A site is counted by θ_W = S/a_n only if at least one observed derived copy survives the per-haplotype quality filter and the subsequent reference imputation. With per-haplotype loss probability f>0 and true derived copy number k_i ≥1,

Pr[ site i is observed as segregating | k_i ] = 1 - f^{k_i} < 1

and the site can be turned into apparent monomorphic reference only, never created. Hence

E[ S_obs ] = Σ_i [1 - f^{k_i}] < Σ_i 1 = S_true

for any fixed f>0. The condition “no completely missing SNV across all samples” is a pre-filtering ascertainment condition on the raw VCF; after the independent per-sample deletions the few remaining derived copies of a low-frequency site can all be the ones that are filtered out in those samples. The site is then scored as monomorphic reference in the imputed haplotypes and is lost from S.

The infinite-sites spectrum is dominated by rare variants. The expected absolute loss Σ_i f^{k_i} = Σ_i f^{i}/i = -log(1-f) >0 is O(1) per unit θ, i.e. a non-vanishing number of singletons and low-frequency sites are removed in expectation. The loss is O(1/log n) relative to a_n, which is why the ratio E[S_obs]/E[S_true] →1 in the mathematical n→∞ limit, but the expectation inequality E[S_obs] < S_true holds for every finite, albeit arbitrarily large, panel. In practice the per-sample filter removes a substantial minority of calls, so the observed set of segregating sites is a proper downward-biased subset of the true segregating set.

Therefore the frequency-independent count S that underlies θ_W is attenuated by the same reference imputation that attenuates allele frequencies, and the frequency-weighted π is attenuated as well. Both θ_W and π are systematically downward biased by random per-sample filtering followed by reference imputation, the bias in π persisting as a constant factor and the bias in θ_W persisting as a non-zero absolute loss of rare segregating sites. That is the usual “both are deflated by missing-as-reference” behaviour.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The ascertained set is the union V of SNVs that are present in at least one haplotype after filtering. With per-haplotype filtering prob f>0, retention r=1-f, for a true site with i≥1 derived copies i'~Bin(i,r). 
Site is lost after reference imputation iff i'=0 with prob f^i.
For infinite-sites spectrum E[#sites with i copies]∝1/i,
E[S_obs]=∑[1-f^i]/i *θ = θ a_n -θ∑f^i/i,
∑f^i/i = -log(1-f)=O(1) finite, while a_n~log n→∞.
Hence E[S_obs]/E[S_true]=1 -[-log(1-f)]/a_n →1 as n→∞.
For any fixed p>0, i=2np→∞ so f^i→0; with the stated no-complete-missing-SNV guarantee, Pr[site remains segregating|p>0]→1. Imputation can only turn derived→reference, never create a new segregating site. Hence on V, θ̂_W=S/a_n is asymptotically preserved; the O(1) loss of ultra-rare singletons is O(1/log n) relative.

Pairwise diversity is frequency dependent.
E[ p̂|p]=r p, 
E[2 p̂(1-p̂)|p]=2 r p[1-r p] <2p(1-p).
Thus E[π̂_i|p]=2 r p[1-r p] < π_i,true, and in rare-variant limit E[π̂]≈r π_true. Thinning persists for n→∞; reference imputation systematically erases derived copies, so nucleotide diversity is downward biased by constant factor r=1-f and does not vanish with sample size.

The majority in both rounds 1 and current round argue B – only π is biased in the arbitrarily large-sample limit, Watterson is asymptotically unbiased for the ascertained variant set. Colleagues 13,14,7 argue C – both are biased because f^i>0 for finite k, rare sites can be rendered monomorphic by sample-specific filtering, so E[S_obs]<S_true for any finite panel and θ_W is formally downward biased. This is a finite-n O(1/log n) effect; the loss is O(1) absolute vs O(log n) segregating sites. The problem explicitly states number of samples is arbitrarily large, so the vanishing relative loss is the relevant limit.

Unresolved nuance: whether “biased” is meant in strict finite-n expectation sense vs asymptotic limit. Under strict finite-n expectation both estimators are downward biased; under the stated arbitrarily-large-n limit the Watterson bias vanishes while π bias remains constant. Current best read is B, i.e. only π remains systematically biased, θ_W is asymptotically unbiased on the ascertained set V.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The ascertained panel is the union V of SNVs that are present in at least one haplotype after per-haplotype quality filtering. Per-haplotype retention is r=1−f, f>0, filtering independent of genotype. After filtering a missing call is imputed to reference 0, so the imputed allele is Y = X R with R∼Bernoulli(r). For a true site with k≥1 derived copies

Pr[site lost after imputation | k]=f^k ,  Pr[segregating] =1−f^k.

E[S_obs] = Σ[1−f^k] = S_true− Σ f^k. Under infinite-sites E[# sites with k copies]∝1/k, so Σ f^k/i = −log(1−f)=O(1) whereas E[S_true]=θ a_{2n}∼θ log n→∞. Hence

E[S_obs]/E[S_true]=1−[−log(1−f)]/a_n →1, and for any fixed p>0, k=2np→∞ ⇒ f^k→0.

Imputation can only turn derived→reference, never create a new segregating site. With the stated no-complete-missing-SNV guarantee, on V S_obs = S_true w.p.1 in the n→∞ limit and

θ̂_W^obs = S_obs / a_n → S_true / a_n = θ̂_W^true,

up to a vanishing O(1/log n) loss of extreme singletons. Frequency-independent presence/absence is asymptotically preserved.

Pairwise diversity is frequency dependent. E[̂p|p]=r p and for two independent haplotypes

E[|Y1−Y2||p]=2 r p[1−r p] <2p(1−p).

Hence per site

E[π̂_i|p]=2 r p[1−r p]=(1−f)π_i,true+O(p^2)<π_i,true,

and in the rare-variant limit E[π̂]/π_true→r=1−f. The thinning of derived copies and systematic replacement of filtered derived alleles by reference removes heterozygosity by the constant factor r, a bias that does not vanish with n.

Majority 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,11,12,15 in round 0/1 therefore conclude B: only π is systematically biased, θ_W is asymptotically unbiased for the ascertained set V. Minority 7,13,14 argue C: the absolute expected loss Σ f^k =−log(1−f)>0 persists for any finite panel, so E[S_obs]<S_true for every realizable n, giving a genuine downward bias in θ_W, most severe for rare variants, in addition to the persistent π bias. The disagreement is asymptotic relative bias vs absolute O(1) bias: relative bias of θ_W is O(1/log n)→0, while π bias is O(1) constant.

Current round reinforces the majority B view with repeated derivations of E[S_obs]/E[S_true]→1 and E[π̂]=rπ_true. Colleague 7 remains the dissenter arguing both estimators are downward biased in any finite arbitrarily large but realizable panel. Unresolved nuance is interpretation of “arbitrarily large” as mathematical limit vs practical finite n.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The per-haplotype quality filter is independent of true genotype with per-haplotype deletion prob. f>0, retention r=1-f. Imputation sets filtered derived alleles to reference: Y_ij = X_ij R_ij, E[ p̂|p]=r p.

*Pi.* E[2 p̂(1-p̂)|p]=2 r p[1-r p] < 2p(1-p). Hence per site heterozygosity is deflated by the r thinning and the p² term from reference imputation. In the rare-variant limit E[π̂]/π≈r. The thinning survives n→∞; pairwise differences are systematically under-estimated by a constant factor for every p>0.

*Segregating sites / Watterson.* A true site with k≥1 derived copies is lost after imputation iff all k copies are filtered: Pr[loss|k]=f^k. Under infinite-sites E[S_obs]=θ Σ(1-f^i)/i = θ a_n - θ Σ f^i/i with Σ f^i/i = -log(1-f)=O(1) while a_n~log n→∞. Hence E[S_obs]/E[S_true]=1- [-log(1-f)]/a_n →1 and for any fixed p>0 f^{2np}→0. With the stated “no SNV is completely missing across all samples’’ ascertainment, on the VCF union V the site is observed segregating with probability 1-f^k→1. In the arbitrarily large n limit S_obs=S_true w.p.1 on V and θ̂_W=S_obs/a_n → θ_W true. The absolute loss of segregating sites is O(1)=-log(1-f), relative loss O(1/log n), vanishing asymptotically.

Hence on the ascertained variant set Watterson’s presence/absence statistic is asymptotically preserved by random reference imputation whereas the frequency-weighted π remains permanently down-biased by r.

Current round reinforces this: colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,11,12,15 give the asymptotic B argument, showing π bias persists and θ_W bias is O(1/log n)→0. Minority 7,13,14 stress finite-n reality: E[S_obs]= Σ[1-f^k]<S_true for any finite n, so both S/a_n and π are downward biased in absolute terms, with the bias in θ_W concentrated on rare variants. The problem explicitly states the number of samples is arbitrarily large, i.e. the n→∞ regime, which makes the asymptotic picture the relevant one: only π stays systematically biased, Watterson is asymptotically unbiased on the ascertained panel. The tension is finite-n absolute loss vs asymptotic relative loss.

The minority C view is correct for strict finite-n expectation, but the large-n statement in the problem favors B. I keep both arguments: asymptotic unbiasedness of θW on V versus finite-n systematic downward loss of rare sites. Current best synthesis is B-only-pi-biased in the stated arbitrarily large-sample limit, with the caveat that finite-n Watterson is formally deflated O(1/log n).

$\displaystyle \frac{E[S_{\rm obs}]}{E[S_{\rm true}]}=1-\frac{-\log(1-f)}{a_{2n}}
 \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1$

and for any fixed $p>0$, $k=2np\to\infty$ so $f^{k}\to0$.
With the stated no-completely-missing-SNV ascertainment $S_{\rm obs}=S_{\rm true}$
w.p.1 on $V$ in the $n\to\infty$ limit.  Watterson

$\hat\theta_{W}=S_{\rm obs}/a_{n}$

is a function of presence/absence only, so on the ascertained set

$\hat\theta_{W}^{\rm obs}=S_{\rm obs}/a_{n}\to S_{\rm true}/a_{n}$
up to the vanishing $O\!\left(1/\log n\right)$ loss of extreme singletons.
Random reference imputation does not create new segregating sites and the
probability of losing the last derived copy vanishes for every fixed $p>0$.

Allele frequency is not preserved. Conditionally on true $p$

$E[\hat p\mid p]=r p$,

and for two independent haplotypes

$E\big[|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|\mid p\big]=2rp\,[1-rp]<2p(1-p)$,

so that per site

$E[\hat\pi_{i}\mid p_{i}]=2rp_{i}[1-rp_{i}]<\!2p_{i}(1-p_{i})$.

Imputation replaces a filtered derived allele by the ancestral reference allele;
pairwise differences are systematically erased by the constant thinning factor
$r=1-f$. In the rare-variant limit $E[\hat\pi]/\pi_{\rm true}\to r<1$ and the
bias persists for every $n$. This is the usual robustness of the
segregating-site count to random missing-as-reference data versus the
non-robustness of a frequency-weighted statistic. On the VCF-ascertained
set $V$ the only non-vanishing systematic bias induced by per-sample random
filtering followed by reference imputation is the downward bias of
nucleotide diversity.

B. Only $\pi$ is biased, $\hat\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically unbiased on the
ascertained variant set in the arbitrarily large-sample limit. The
finite-$n$ $O(1/\log n)$ loss of $S$ is a real finite-sample downward
attenuation, vanishing relatively as $n\to\infty$.

2.text:
The set on which the estimators are evaluated is the VCF ascertained union
$V$ of true SNVs. Let $f>0$ be the per haplotype per site probability that a
true derived call is quality filtered and then imputed to the reference and
$r=1-f$ the retention probability. With $k\ge1$ true derived copies at a site,
$K\sim {\rm Bin}(k,r)$ is the number of derived copies that survive the
filter and

${\rm Pr}\{ K=0\mid k\}=f^{k}$ ,
${\rm Pr}\{ {\rm site\;segregating\;after\;imputation}\mid k\}=1-f^{k}.$

Reference imputation can only turn a derived allele into the ancestral
allele, it can never create a new segregating site.

Segregation / Watterson. On $V$

$E[S_{\rm obs}]=\sum_{i\in V}\bigl[1-f^{k_{i}}\bigr]=|V|-\sum_{i}f^{k_{i}}.$

Under the infinite-sites spectrum $E[\#i\mid k]\propto 1/k$ so that

$\sum_{i}f^{k_{i}}\propto\sum_{k\ge1}f^{k}/k=-\log(1-f)=O(1)$

whereas $E[S_{\rm true}]=|V|=\theta a_{2n}$ with $a_{2n}\sim\log n\to\infty$.
Hence

$\frac{E[S_{\rm obs}]}{E[S_{\rm true}]}=
1-\frac{-\log(1-f)}{a_{2n}}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1,$

and for any fixed $p>0$, $k=2np\to\infty$ so $f^{k}\to0$. With the
no-complete-missing-SNV ascertainment ${\rm Pr}\{K>0\mid p>0\}\to1$ and
$S_{\rm obs}=S_{\rm true}$ w.p.1 on $V$ in the large $n$ limit. Watterson

$\hat\theta_{W}=S_{\rm obs}/a_{n}$

is a function of presence/absence only. Up to the $O(1/\log n)$ loss of
extreme singletons the presence/absence information is asymptotically
preserved by random reference imputation. On the ascertained set $V$
$\hat\theta_{W}^{\rm obs}\xrightarrow{p}\hat\theta_{W}^{\rm true}$, i.e.
the site-count statistic is asymptotically unbiased in the arbitrarily
large-sample regime stated.

Pairwise diversity. Conditional on a true derived frequency $p$,

$E[\hat p\mid p]=r p$,

so for two independent haplotypes

$E[|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|\mid p]=2rp[1-rp]<2p(1-p)$.

Hence per site

$E[\hat\pi_{i}\mid p]=2rp[1-rp]<2p(1-p)=\pi_{i}^{\rm true},$

and in the rare-variant limit $E[\hat\pi_{i}]\approx r\,\pi_{i}^{\rm true}$.
Reference imputation systematically erases the filtered derived copies,
$p\to rp$, and the attenuation by the constant factor $r=1-f$ persists for
every $p>0$ and does not vanish as $n\to\infty$.

Thus on the VCF ascertained panel the frequency independent segregating-site
count, and hence $\theta_{W}$, is asymptotically preserved while the
frequency weighted nucleotide diversity remains systematically downward biased
by the random deletion+reference imputation.  Strictly finite $n$ both
estimators are formally downward biased, the Watterson bias being the
vanishing $O(1/\log n)$ loss of rare sites; in the arbitrarily large sample
limit described the only non-vanishing systematic bias is that of $\pi$.

B. Only pi, nucleotide diversity, is biased, $\hat\theta_{W}$ is
asymptotically unbiased on the ascertained variant set.

8.text:
On the union V of SNVs that is analysed the per-haplotype filtering is an
independent thinning with retention $r=1-f>0$, $f>0$.

For a true site with $k\ge1$ derived copies in $2n$ haplotypes, $p=k/2n$,

$K\mid k\sim {\rm Bin}(k,r), \qquad {\rm Pr}[K=0\mid k]=f^{\,k}$.

Imputation to reference sets the haplotype to $0$ whenever the call is
deleted, so a site can only go from segregating to monomorphic, never the
reverse. Watterson uses only presence/absence,

$\hat\theta_{W}=S_{\rm obs}/a_{n},\qquad a_{n}=\sum_{i<n}i^{-1}$.

${\rm Pr}\{ {\rm site\;observed\;segregating}\mid k\}=1-f^{k}$ and under
infinite sites

$E[S_{\rm obs}]= \sum_{k\ge1}\frac{1-f^{k}}{k}\,\theta$,
$E[S_{\rm true}]=\theta a_{2n}$.

$\sum_{k\ge1}f^{k}/k=-\log(1-f)<\infty$ whereas $a_{2n}\sim\log n\to\infty$,
so

$E[S_{\rm obs}]/E[S_{\rm true}]=1-\frac{-\log(1-f)}{a_{2n}}\to1$,

and for any fixed $p>0$, $k=2np\to\infty$ and $f^{k}\to0$.  With the stated
no-complete-missing-SNV ascertainment a truly segregating site is lost
with probability $f^{k}\to0$ and on the ascertained VCF set $V$

$S_{\rm obs}=S_{\rm true}$ w.p.1 in the $n\to\infty$ limit.  Imputation to
reference can never create a new segregating site, so the $0/1$ information
on which $S/a_{n}$ is based is asymptotically preserved.  The $O(1)$
absolute loss $-\log(1-f)$ of very rare singletons is $O(1/\log n)$
relative to $S_{\rm true}$ and vanishes in the arbitrarily large sample
limit.

Nucleotide diversity is frequency weighted.  Conditional on true $p$,

$E[\hat p\mid p]=r p$,
$E[|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|\mid p]=2rp[1-rp]<2p(1-p)$.

Hence per site

$E[\hat\pi_{i}\mid p_{i}]=2rp_{i}[1-rp_{i}]<\pi_{i}^{\rm true}$,

so that $E[\hat\pi_{obs}]\approx r\,\pi_{\rm true}$ in the rare variant
limit.  The thinning $p\to rp$ and the systematic replacement of deleted
derived copies by the reference allele erases heterozygosity by the constant
factor $r$ for every $p>0$ and the bias does not vanish with $n$.

On the ascertained variant set $V$ the counting statistic $\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$
is asymptotically preserved by random reference imputation whereas the
frequency dependent $\pi$ remains systematically downward biased by the
$r$ attenuation.  This is the usual robustness of Watterson’s
segregating-site count to random missing-as-reference data versus the
non-robustness of $\pi$.

B. Only $\pi$ is biased in the arbitrarily large-sample limit; $\hat\theta_{W}$
is asymptotically unbiased on the ascertained set, the finite-$n$ $O(1/\log n)$
loss of extreme singletons being the conventional finite-sample artefact.

6.text:
The sites that are analysed are the union $V$ of true SNVs.  Write $f>0$
for the per haplotype loss probability and $r=1-f$ for retention.  After
the per-haplotype quality filter and reference imputation

$Y_{ij}=X_{ij}R_{ij},\qquad R_{ij}\sim{\rm Bern}(r)$

so that for a true site with $k\ge1$ derived copies in $2n$ haplotypes

${\rm Pr}\{Y\;{\rm is\;monomorphic}\mid k\}=f^{\,k},\qquad
 {\rm Pr}\{Y\;{\rm segregating}\mid k\}=1-f^{\,k}$.

Reference imputation can only turn a derived allele into reference, it can
never create a segregating site.

Segregating-site count.  With the infinite-sites spectrum
$E[\#{\rm sites\;with\;k}]\propto1/k$

$$
E[S_{\rm obs}]=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{1-f^{k}}{k}\,\theta
   =\theta a_{2n}-\theta\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{f^{k}}{k},
\qquad a_{2n}=\sum_{i\le2n}1/i\sim\log n,
$$

$$
\sum_{k\ge1}f^{k}/k=-\log(1-f)=O(1).
$$

Hence

$$
\frac{E[S_{\rm obs}]}{E[S_{\rm true}]}=
1-\frac{-\log(1-f)}{a_{2n}}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1,
$$

and for any fixed $p>0$, $k=2np\to\infty$ so $f^{k}\to0$.  With the
no-complete-missing-SNV ascertainment the site is observed segregating
w.p. $1-f^{k}\to1$.  $S_{\rm obs}=S_{\rm true}$ w.p.1 on $V$ in the
$n\to\infty$ limit and

$$
\hat\theta_{W}^{\rm obs}=S_{\rm obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow{p}
S_{\rm true}/a_{n}=\hat\theta_{W}^{\rm true},
$$

i.e. the presence/absence information on which Watterson’s estimator is
based is asymptotically preserved.  The absolute $O(1)$ loss of the rarest
sites is $O(1/\log n)$ relative to $S_{\rm true}$ and vanishes in the
arbitrarily large sample limit stated.

Pairwise diversity is frequency weighted. Conditional on true derived
frequency $p$

$$
E[\hat p\mid p]=rp,
$$

so for two independent haplotypes

$$
E[|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|\mid p]=2rp\,[1-rp]<2p(1-p),\qquad0<r<1 .
$$

Hence per site

$$
E[\hat\pi_{i}\mid p_{i}]=2rp_{i}[1-rp_{i}]
<(1-f)2p_{i}(1-p_{i})<2p_{i}(1-p_{i}),
$$

and

$$
E[\hat\pi_{\rm obs}]
=\sum_{i\in V}2rp_{i}[1-rp_{i}]
<(1-f)\sum_{i\in V}2p_{i}(1-p_{i})=\pi_{\rm true},
$$

with $E[\hat\pi]/\pi\to r$ in the rare-variant limit. The thinning
$p\to rp$ and the systematic replacement of deleted derived copies by the
reference allele persist for every $p>0$ and for $n\to\infty$.  Nucleotide
diversity is therefore systematically downward biased by the constant
factor $r=1-f$, the usual non-robustness of a frequency weighted statistic
to missing-as-reference data.

On the ascertained variant set $V$ the frequency independent count $S/a_{n}$
is asymptotically unbiased in the arbitrarily large sample limit while
$\pi$ remains persistently downward biased.  Finite $n$ the $O(1)$ loss
$\sum f^{k}/k$ gives a formally $O(1/\log n)$ downward finite-sample bias
in $\theta_{W}$, the non-vanishing systematic bias that remains in the
limit described is that of $\pi$.

B. Only $\pi$ is biased; $\hat\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically preserved on
the ascertained VCF set.

11.text:
The sites that can be scored are the union $V$ of SNVs that are present in at least one
haplotype before the per-sample quality filter.  Let $f>0$ be the per haplotype
per site loss probability and $r=1-f$ the retention probability and let a true
site have $k\ge1$ derived copies in $2n$ haplotypes, $p=k/2n$.
After independent thinning and reference imputation

$Y_{ij}=X_{ij}R_{ij}$ , $R_{ij}\sim{\rm Bern}(r)$ independent of $X_{ij}$,

so that $E[\hat p\mid p]=rp$ and a site is seen as segregating after
imputation iff $K>0$ where $K\sim{\rm Bin}(k,r)$,

${\rm Pr}\{K=0\mid k\}=f^{k},\qquad {\rm Pr}\{{\rm segregating}\mid k\}=1-f^{k}$.

Segregation is a $0/1$ property.  With the infinite-sites neutral spectrum
$E[\#{\rm sites\;with\;k\;copies}]\propto k^{-1}$

$E[S_{\rm obs}]=\sum_{s}[1-f^{k_{s}}]
 =E[S_{\rm true}]-\sum_{k\ge1}c\,f^{k}k^{-1}$,

$\sum_{k\ge1}f^{k}/k=-\log (1-f)=O(1)$ whereas
$E[S_{\rm true}]=\theta a_{2n}$ with $a_{2n}=\sum_{i\le2n}i^{-1}\sim\log n\to\infty$.
Hence

$\displaystyle\frac{E[S_{\rm obs}]}{E[S_{\rm true}]}
 =1-\frac{-\log(1-f)}{a_{2n}}\to1,$

and for any fixed $p>0$, $k=2np\to\infty$ so $f^{k}\to0$.  With the
no-complete-missing-SNV ascertainment the site is observed as segregating
with probability $1-f^{k}\to1$.  Imputation to the reference can only turn
derived $\to$ reference, it can never create a new segregating site, so on the
ascertained set $V$

$\hat\theta_{W}^{\rm obs}=S_{\rm obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow{p}
S_{\rm true}/a_{n}=\hat\theta_{W}^{\rm true}$

up to the vanishing $O\!\left(-\log(1-f)/a_{n}\right)=O(1/\log n)$ loss of the
very rare singletons.  In the arbitrarily large-sample limit stated the
presence/absence count $S$ and hence Watterson’s $\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$ is
asymptotically preserved by random reference imputation.

Nucleotide diversity is frequency weighted.  Conditional on $p$

$E[\hat p\mid p]=rp$,

$E\bigl[|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|\mid p\bigr]=2rp\,[1-rp]<2p(1-p)$,

so that per site

$E[\hat\pi_{i}\mid p_{i}]=2rp_{i}[1-rp_{i}]<2p_{i}(1-p_{i})$,

and in the rare-variant limit $E[\hat\pi_{i}]\approx r\,\pi_{i}^{\rm true}$.
The thinning $p\to rp$ and the systematic replacement of deleted derived
copies by the reference allele deflate pairwise differences by the constant
factor $r=1-f$ for every $p>0$ and the bias does not vanish with $n$.
Hence $\hat\pi_{V}$ remains systematically downward biased by reference
imputation whereas the site-count statistic $\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically
unbiased on the ascertained variant set.  That is the usual robustness of
Watterson’s $S/a_{n}$ to random missing-as-reference versus the
non-robustness of $\pi$.

Strictly finite $n$, $E[S_{\rm obs}]<E[S_{\rm true}]$ by the $O(1)$ loss
$-\log(1-f)$, i.e. an $O(1/\log n)$ downward bias in $\theta_{W}$, which
vanishes relatively as $n\to\infty$.  The persistent, non-vanishing bias in
the arbitrarily large-sample limit is that of $\pi$.

B. Only pi (nucleotide diversity) is biased, Watterson’s $\theta_{W}$ is
asymptotically preserved on the ascertained SNV set.

3.text:
With the VCF-union $V$ let $f>0$ be the per haplotype deletion probability,
$r=1-f$, and let a true site have $k\ge 1$ derived copies in $2n$ haplotypes,
$p=k/2n$.  After independent quality filtering and reference imputation

$Y_{ij}=X_{ij}R_{ij},\qquad R_{ij}\sim{\rm Bernoulli}(r)$,

so that $E[\hat p\mid p]=rp$ and the observed copy number is
$K\sim{\rm Bin}(k,r)$.  

Segregation is $0/1$.  A truly segregating site is scored monomorphic after
imputation iff $K=0$,

$\Pr\{K=0\mid k\}=f^{k},\qquad \Pr\{{\rm segregating}\mid k\}=1-f^{k}$,

so that on $V$

$E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{s\in V}\!\left[1-f^{k_{s}}\right]
      =S_{true}-\sum_{s}f^{k_{s}}$.
Under infinite sites $E[\#\{k\}]\propto 1/k$ and

$\sum_{s}f^{k_{s}}= \sum_{k\ge1}\frac{f^{k}}{k}=-\log(1-f)=O(1)$

whereas $E[S_{true}]=\theta a_{2n}$ with
$a_{2n}=\sum_{i\le2n}i^{-1}\sim\log n\to\infty$. Hence

$\displaystyle
\frac{E[S_{obs}]}{E[S_{true}]}=
1-\frac{-\log(1-f)}{a_{2n}}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1,
$

and for any fixed $p>0$, $k=2np\to\infty$ and $f^{k}\to0$.
With the stated no-complete-missing-SNV ascertainment
$\Pr\{Y\text{ segregating}\mid p>0\}=1-f^{k}\to1$ and
$S_{obs}=S_{true}$ w.p.1 on $V$ in the $n\to\infty$ limit.  Imputation to
reference can only turn derived$\to$reference, it can never create a new
segregating site, so

$\hat\theta_{W}^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow{p}
S_{true}/a_{n}=\hat\theta_{W}^{true}$

up to the $O(1/\log n)$ loss of the extreme singletons.  The
presence/absence information on which Watterson’s $S/a_{n}$ is based is
asymptotically preserved by random reference imputation.

Frequency is not preserved.  For a site

$E[\hat p\mid p]=rp$,

and for two independent haplotypes

$E[|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|\mid p]=2rp[1-rp]<2p(1-p)$,

so that per site

$E[\hat\pi_{i}\mid p_{i}]
   =2rp_{i}[1-rp_{i}]
   =(1-f)\,\pi_{i}^{\rm true}+O(p_{i}^{2})<\pi_{i}^{\rm true}$,

and in the rare-variant limit $E[\hat\pi]/\pi_{true}\to r=1-f$.
The thinning $p\to rp$ and the systematic replacement of the filtered
derived copies by the reference allele removes heterozygosity by the constant
factor $r$ for every $p>0$ and the bias does not vanish with $n$.

Hence on the ascertained SNV set $V$ the frequency-independent segregating-
site count, and therefore Watterson’s $\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$, is asymptotically
unbiased in the arbitrarily large-sample limit, while nucleotide diversity
$\pi$ remains systematically downward biased by the $1-f$ reference
imputation.  In strict finite-$n$ terms $E[S_{obs}]<E[S_{true}]$, i.e. an
$O(1/\log n)$ downward $S$ loss, but the non-vanishing systematic bias in
the limit described is that of $\pi$ only.

B. Only $\pi$ is biased; $\hat\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically unbiased on the
ascertained variant set.

E[ p̂ | p ] = r p

Pr[ site seen | k ] = 1 - f^k < 1

E[S_obs] = Σ_i [1 - f^{k_i}] < Σ_i 1 = S_true

E[ p̂ | p ] = (1-f)p,
E[2p̂(1-p̂) | p] = 2(1-f)p[1-(1-f)p] < 2p(1-p),

${\rm Pr}\{Y\;{\rm is\;monomorphic}\mid k\}=f^{\,k},\qquad
 {\rm Pr}\{Y\;{\rm segregating}\mid k\}=1-f^{\,k}$.

Reference imputation can only turn a derived allele into reference, it can
never create a segregating site.

Segregating-site count.  With the infinite-sites spectrum
$E[\#{\rm sites\;with\;k}]\propto1/k$

$$
E[S_{\rm obs}]=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{1-f^{k}}{k}\,\theta
   =\theta a_{2n}-\theta\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{f^{k}}{k},
\qquad a_{2n}=\sum_{i\le2n}1/i\sim\log n,
$$

$$
\sum_{k\ge1}f^{k}/k=-\log(1-f)=O(1).
$$

Hence

$$
\frac{E[S_{\rm obs}]}{E[S_{\rm true}]}=
1-\frac{-\log(1-f)}{a_{2n}}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1,
$$

and for any fixed $p>0$, $k=2np\to\infty$ so $f^{k}\to0$.  With the
no-complete-missing-SNV ascertainment the site is observed segregating
w.p. $1-f^{k}\to1$.  $S_{\rm obs}=S_{\rm true}$ w.p.1 on $V$ in the
$n\to\infty$ limit and

$$
\hat\theta_{W}^{\rm obs}=S_{\rm obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow{p}
S_{\rm true}/a_{n}=\hat\theta_{W}^{\rm true},
$$

i.e. the presence/absence information on which Watterson’s estimator is
based is asymptotically preserved.  The absolute $O(1)$ loss of the rarest
sites is $O(1/\log n)$ relative to $S_{\rm true}$ and vanishes in the
arbitrarily large sample limit stated.

Pairwise diversity is frequency weighted. Conditional on true derived
frequency $p$

$$
E[\hat p\mid p]=rp,
$$

so for two independent haplotypes

$$
E[|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|\mid p]=2rp\,[1-rp]<2p(1-p),\qquad0<r<1 .
$$

Hence per site

$$
E[\hat\pi_{i}\mid p_{i}]=2rp_{i}[1-rp_{i}]
<(1-f)2p_{i}(1-p_{i})<2p_{i}(1-p_{i}),
$$

and

$$
E[\hat\pi_{\rm obs}]
=\sum_{i\in V}2rp_{i}[1-rp_{i}]
<(1-f)\sum_{i\in V}2p_{i}(1-p_{i})=\pi_{\rm true},
$$

with $E[\hat\pi]/\pi\to r$ in the rare-variant limit. The thinning
$p\to rp$ and the systematic replacement of deleted derived copies by the
reference allele persist for every $p>0$ and for $n\to\infty$.  Nucleotide
diversity is therefore systematically downward biased by the constant
factor $r=1-f$, the usual non-robustness of a frequency weighted statistic
to missing-as-reference data.

On the ascertained variant set $V$ the frequency independent count $S/a_{n}$
is asymptotically unbiased in the arbitrarily large sample limit while
$\pi$ remains persistently downward biased.  Finite $n$ the $O(1)$ loss
$\sum f^{k}/k$ gives a formally $O(1/\log n)$ downward finite-sample bias
in $\theta_{W}$, the non-vanishing systematic bias that remains in the
limit described is that of $\pi$.

B. Only $\pi$ is biased; $\hat\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically preserved on
the ascertained VCF set.

With the VCF-union $V$ let $f>0$ be the per haplotype deletion probability,
$r=1-f$, and let a true site have $k\ge 1$ derived copies in $2n$ haplotypes,

$Y_{ij}=X_{ij}R_{ij},\qquad R_{ij}\sim{\rm Bernoulli}(r)$,

so that $E[\hat p\mid p]=rp$ and the observed copy number is
$K\sim{\rm Bin}(k,r)$.  

Segregation is $0/1$.  A truly segregating site is scored monomorphic after
imputation iff $K=0$,

$\Pr\{K=0\mid k\}=f^{k},\qquad \Pr\{{\rm segregating}\mid k\}=1-f^{k}$,

so that on $V$

$E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{s\in V}\!\left[1-f^{k_{s}}\right]
      =S_{true}-\sum_{s}f^{k_{s}}$.
Under infinite sites $E[\#\{k\}]\propto 1/k$ and

$\sum_{s}f^{k_{s}}= \sum_{k\ge1}\frac{f^{k}}{k}=-\log(1-f)=O(1)$

whereas $E[S_{true}]=\theta a_{2n}$ with
$a_{2n}=\sum_{i\le2n}i^{-1}\sim\log n\to\infty$. Hence

$\displaystyle
\frac{E[S_{obs}]}{E[S_{true}]}=
1-\frac{-\log(1-f)}{a_{2n}}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1,
$

and for any fixed $p>0$, $k=2np\to\infty$ and $f^{k}\to0$.
With the stated no-complete-missing-SNV ascertainment
$\Pr\{Y\text{ segregating}\mid p>0\}=1-f^{k}\to1$ and
$S_{obs}=S_{true}$ w.p.1 on $V$ in the $n\to\infty$ limit.  Imputation to
reference can only turn derived$\to$reference, it can never create a new
segregating site, so

$\hat\theta_{W}^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow{p}
S_{true}/a_{n}=\hat\theta_{W}^{true}$

up to the $O(1/\log n)$ loss of the extreme singletons.  The
presence/absence information on which Watterson’s $S/a_{n}$ is based is
asymptotically preserved by random reference imputation.

Frequency is not preserved.  For a site

$E[\hat p\mid p]=rp$,

and for two independent haplotypes

$E[|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|\mid p]=2rp[1-rp]<2p(1-p)$,

so that per site

$E[\hat\pi_{i}\mid p_{i}]
   =2rp_{i}[1-rp_{i}]
   =(1-f)\,\pi_{i}^{\rm true}+O(p_{i}^{2})<\pi_{i}^{\rm true}$,

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The ascertained set is the VCF union V of sites that are true SNVs and are observed in ≥1 haplotype before filtering, with the stated “no SNV completely missing across all samples’’ pre-filter ascertainment. Per-haplotype deletion probability f>0, retention r=1-f, independent of true genotype. After reference imputation Y_ij = X_ij R_ij with R_ij~Bern(r), E[p̂|p]= r p.

*π.* For two independent haplotypes E[|Y1-Y2||p]=2 r p[1-r p] <2p(1-p). Per site E[π̂_i|p]=2 r p[1-r p]≈ r 2p for rare variants. The thinning p→r p and the systematic replacement of filtered derived copies by reference removes heterozygosity by the constant factor r. E[π̂]/π≈ r in the rare-variant limit and the bias persists for every p>0 and for n→∞.

*Watterson.* A true site with k≥1 derived copies is lost after imputation iff all k copies are filtered: Pr[loss|k]=f^k, Pr[segregating|k]=1-f^k. Hence E[S_obs]= Σ[1-f^k]. Under infinite-sites E[#sites with k]∝1/k, Σ f^k/k = -log(1-f)=O(1) whereas E[S_true]=θ a_n with a_n=∑1/i∼log n→∞. So E[S_obs]/E[S_true]=1-[-log(1-f)]/a_n→1, and for any fixed p>0, k=2 n p→∞ so f^k→0. Reference imputation can only turn derived→reference, never create a new segregating site. On V, S_obs=S_true w.p.1 in the n→∞ limit and θ̂_W=S_obs/a_n→S_true/a_n. The absolute loss is O(1)=-log(1-f), relative loss O(1/log n), vanishing asymptotically.

Unresolved: wording of “biased’’ as absolute finite-sample expectation vs asymptotic limit. Consensus in this round for the stated arbitrarily large-sample limit is B. Only π biased; Watterson is asymptotically unbiased on the ascertained variant set.

3.text:
On the ascertained union $V$ of true SNVs that are present in at least one
haplotype before filtering let $f>0$ be the per-haplotype loss probability
and $r=1-f$ the retention probability. After independent quality filtering
and reference imputation

$Y_{ij}=X_{ij}R_{ij}$ , $R_{ij}\sim{\rm Bern}(r)$

so that for a true site with $k\ge1$ derived copies in $2n$ haplotypes
$p=k/2n$

$K\mid k\sim{\rm Bin}(k,r)$, ${\rm Pr}\{K=0\mid k\}=f^{k}$,
${\rm Pr}\{{\rm segregating\;after\;imputation}\mid k\}=1-f^{k}$.

Reference imputation can only turn derived $\to$ reference, it can never
create a new segregating site.

* Segregation / Watterson.
$E[S_{\rm obs}]=\sum_{s}[1-f^{k_{s}}]=S_{\rm true}-\sum_{s}f^{k_{s}}$.
Under infinite sites $E[\#{\rm sites\;with\;k}]\propto k^{-1}$,

$\sum_{s}f^{k_{s}}\propto\sum_{k\ge1}f^{k}/k=-\log(1-f)=O(1)$

whereas $E[S_{\rm true}]=\theta a_{2n}$ with $a_{2n}=\sum_{i\le2n}i^{-1}
\sim\log n\to\infty$. Hence

$\displaystyle\frac{E[S_{\rm obs}]}{E[S_{\rm true}]}=
1-\frac{-\log(1-f)}{a_{2n}}\to1,$

and for any fixed $p>0$, $k=2np\to\infty$ so $f^{k}\to0$. With the stated
no-completely-missing-SNV ascertainment a truly segregating site is lost
with probability $f^{k}\to0$ and $S_{\rm obs}=S_{\rm true}$ w.p.1 on $V$
in the $n\to\infty$ limit. Watterson’s estimator is a $0/1$ statistic

$\hat\theta_{W}=S_{\rm obs}/a_{n}$,

so on $V$

$\hat\theta_{W}^{\rm obs}=S_{\rm obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow{p}
S_{\rm true}/a_{n}=\hat\theta_{W}^{\rm true}$

up to the vanishing $O\!\left(-\log(1-f)/a_{n}\right)=O(1/\log n)$ loss of
extreme singletons. Presence/absence is asymptotically preserved by random
missing-as-reference.

* Nucleotide diversity.
$E[\hat p\mid p]=rp$ and for two independent haplotypes

$E[|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|\mid p]=2rp[1-rp]<2p(1-p)$.

Hence per site

$E[\hat\pi_{i}\mid p_{i}]=2rp_{i}[1-rp_{i}]<2p_{i}(1-p_{i})$,

and in the rare-variant limit $E[\hat\pi_{i}]\approx r\,\pi_{i}^{\rm true}$.
The thinning $p\to rp$ and the systematic replacement of the filtered
derived copies by the reference allele removes heterozygosity by the
constant factor $r=1-f$ for every $p>0$ and the bias does not vanish with
$n$.

On the VCF-ascertained SNV panel the frequency independent segregating-site
count, and therefore $\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$, is asymptotically preserved in
the arbitrarily large-sample limit stated, whereas $\pi$ remains
systematically downward deflated by reference imputation. The finite-$n$
$O(1)$ absolute loss $-\log(1-f)$ of rare sites is $O(1/\log n)$ relative
and vanishes in the limit.

asymptotically unbiased on the ascertained variant set.

The numerator is systematically depleted by reference imputation: a low frequency site can lose all of its remaining derived copies in the imputed haplotypes and be called monomorphic reference, even though the raw VCF was ascertained pre-filtering to have no completely missing SNV. The no-missing-SNV guarantee is a pre-filtering ascertainment property of the raw VCF. After sample-specific random deletion and reference imputation the site frequency spectrum keeps feeding in new k=1,2,… sites as the panel grows, so there is always a non-vanishing fraction of sites with bounded k for which f^k is not negligible.

Hence in any finite albeit arbitrarily large panel we have E[S_obs] < S_true and E[θ̂_W^obs] = E[S_obs]/a_n < θ. The bias is small relative to a_n but it is a real systematic downward bias in the count statistic that underlies θ_W, exactly the same direction as for π.

For π the situation is starker: E[|Y1-Y2||p] = 2 r p[1 - r p] < 2p(1-p) for every p>0 and E[π̂] ≈ r π_true in the rare variant limit, so the frequency-weighted bias persists even in the limit.

In practice we compute both estimators from the imputed data, i.e. from a downward biased site count and downward biased allele frequencies. Reference imputation therefore deflates both the presence/absence statistic used by Watterson and the frequency-weighted statistic π, with π being more severely and persistently affected. That is the conservative finite-sample picture I think the prompt is asking for.

C. Both Watterson’s estimator and π are systematically downward biased by random per-sample filtering followed by reference imputation.

The analysable set is the pre-filtering VCF union

$V=\{i:k_{i}\ge1\}$

with per haplotype retention $r=1-f>0$. After filtering and reference
imputation

$Y_{ij}=X_{ij}R_{ij},\qquad R_{ij}\sim{\rm Bern}(r)$

so for a true site with $k\ge1$ derived copies, $p=k/2n$,

${\rm Pr}\{Y\;{\rm monomorphic}\mid k\}=f^{k},\qquad
{\rm Pr}\{Y\;{\rm segregating}\mid k\}=1-f^{k}$.

Imputation can only turn derived $\to$ reference, it can never create a new
segregating site.  Segregation is $0/1$ so

$E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{s\in V}\bigl[1-f^{k_{s}}\bigr]
=E[S_{true}]-\sum_{s}f^{k_{s}}.$

With the infinite sites spectrum $E[\#{\rm sites\;with\;k}]\propto k^{-1}$

$\sum_{s}f^{k_{s}}\propto\sum_{k\ge1}f^{k}/k=-\log(1-f)=O(1)$

whereas $E[S_{true}]=\theta a_{2n}$ with $a_{2n}=\sum_{i\le2n}i^{-1}\sim
\log n\to\infty$. Hence

$\frac{E[S_{obs}]}{E[S_{true}]}=1-\frac{-\log(1-f)}{a_{2n}}\to1,$

and for any fixed $p>0$, $k=2np\to\infty$ so $f^{k}\to0$. With the
no-completely-missing-SNV ascertainment ${\rm Pr}\{K>0\mid p>0\}\to1$ and
$S_{obs}=S_{true}$ w.p.1 on $V$ in the $n\to\infty$ limit.  Watterson

$\hat\theta_{W}=S_{obs}/a_{n}$

is a function of presence/absence only, so on the ascertained set

$\hat\theta_{W}^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow{p}
S_{true}/a_{n}=\hat\theta_{W}^{true}$

up to the vanishing $O\!\left(-\log(1-f)/a_{n}\right)=O(1/\log n)$ loss of
extreme singletons. The $O(1)$ absolute loss $-\log(1-f)$ is negligible
relative to $S_{true}=O(\log n)$ in the arbitrarily large sample limit
stated. The $0/1$ site count is asymptotically preserved by random
missing-as-reference.

Frequency is not preserved.  Conditional on true $p$,

$E[\hat p\mid p]=r p$,

and for two independent haplotypes

$E[|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|\mid p]=2rp[1-rp]<2p(1-p)$.

Per site

$E[\hat\pi_{i}\mid p_{i}]=2rp_{i}[1-rp_{i}]<2p_{i}(1-p_{i})$,

and in the rare variant limit $E[\hat\pi_{i}]\approx r\,\pi_{i}^{\rm true}$.
The thinning $p\to rp$ and the systematic replacement of deleted derived
copies by the reference allele deflates heterozygosity by the constant
factor $r=1-f$ for every $p>0$ and the bias does not vanish as $n\to\infty$.

Hence on the VCF-ascertained SNV panel the frequency independent
segregating-site count and therefore $\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$ is asymptotically
unbiased in the arbitrarily large-sample regime, whereas nucleotide
diversity remains systematically downward biased by the $r$ attenuation.
In strict finite-$n$ terms $E[S_{obs}]<E[S_{true}]$ by the $O(1)$ term
$-\log(1-f)$, i.e. an $O(1/\log n)$ finite-sample downward bias in
$\theta_{W}$, which vanishes relatively as $n\to\infty$.

B. Only $\pi$ is persistently biased; $\hat\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically
unbiased on the ascertained variant set in the stated $n\to\infty$ limit.

$E[S_{\rm obs}]=\sum_{s\in V}[1-f^{k_{s}}]=S_{\rm true}-\sum_{s}f^{k_{s}}$.

$\sum_{s}f^{k_{s}}\propto\sum_{k\ge1}f^{k}/k=-\log(1-f)=O(1)$,

11.text:
On the pre-filtering VCF union $V$ let $f>0$ be the per-haplotype per-site loss
probability and $r=1-f$ the retention probability, $R_{ij}\sim{\rm Bern}(r)$
independent of the true genotype $X_{ij}$. After quality filtering and
reference imputation

$Y_{ij}=X_{ij}R_{ij}$,

so a filtered derived copy is set to the reference allele. Imputation can
only turn derived $\to$ reference, it can never create a new segregating site.

For a true site with $k\ge1$ derived copies in $2n$ haplotypes, $p=k/2n$,

${\rm Pr}\{K=0\mid k\}=f^{k},\qquad {\rm Pr}\{{\rm segregating\;after\;imputation}\mid k\}=1-f^{k}$.

$E[\hat p\mid p]=rp$.

Segregation / Watterson. On $V$

$E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{s}[1-f^{k_{s}}]=S_{true}-\sum_{s}f^{k_{s}}$.

With infinite sites $E[\#{\rm sites\;with\;k}]\propto k^{-1}$,

$\sum_{s}f^{k_{s}}\propto\sum_{k\ge1}f^{k}/k=-\log(1-f)=O(1)$

whereas $E[S_{true}]=\theta a_{n}$ with $a_{n}=\sum_{i<n}i^{-1}\sim\log n\to\infty$.
Hence

$\displaystyle\frac{E[S_{obs}]}{E[S_{true}]}=1-\frac{-\log(1-f)}{a_{n}}\to1$,
and for any fixed $p>0$, $k=2np\to\infty$ so $f^{k}\to0$.
With the stated no-completely-missing-SNV ascertainment a truly
segregating site is lost with probability $f^{k}\to0$ and
$S_{obs}=S_{true}$ w.p.1 on $V$ in the $n\to\infty$ limit.

Watterson is a $0/1$ presence/absence statistic
$\hat\theta_{W}=S_{obs}/a_{n}$, so on $V$

$\hat\theta_{W}^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}/a_{n}
=\hat\theta_{W}^{true}$

up to the vanishing $O\!\left(-\log(1-f)/a_{n}\right)=O(1/\log n)$ loss of
extreme singletons. The $O(1)$ absolute loss $-\log(1-f)$ is negligible
relative to $a_{n}$ in the arbitrarily large-sample regime stated.
Presence/absence is asymptotically preserved by random missing-as-reference.

Pairwise diversity is frequency weighted. Conditional on true $p$,

$E[|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|\mid p]=2rp[1-rp]<2p(1-p)$,

so per site

$E[\hat\pi_{i}\mid p_{i}]=2rp_{i}[1-rp_{i}]<2p_{i}(1-p_{i})$,

and in the rare-variant limit $E[\hat\pi_{i}]\approx r\,\pi_{i}^{true}$.
The thinning $p\to rp$ and the systematic replacement of filtered derived
copies by the reference allele deflates heterozygosity by the constant
factor $r=1-f$ for every $p>0$ and the bias does not vanish with $n$.

Hence on the ascertained SNV panel $V$ the frequency-independent count
$S/a_{n}$ and therefore Watterson’s $\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically
preserved by random reference imputation in the arbitrarily large sample
limit, whereas nucleotide diversity remains systematically downward biased
by the $r$ attenuation.

is asymptotically unbiased on the ascertained variant set. Strictly finite
$n$, $E[S_{obs}]<E[S_{true}]$ by the $O(1)$ term $-\log(1-f)$, i.e. an
$O(1/\log n)$ finite-sample downward attenuation of $\theta_{W}$, which
vanishes relatively as $n\to\infty$.

whereas $E[S_{true}]=\theta a_{2n}$ with $a_{2n}=\sum_{i\le2n}i^{-1}\sim\log n\to\infty$.

for every realisable panel. With the infinite-sites spectrum E[#sites with k]∝1/k,

That limit is mathematically correct but it is not the calculation we actually perform. The prompt describes an arbitrarily large but finite panel, with per-sample random quality filtering and reference imputation, and the estimators are computed from the imputed sequences we actually obtain. The no-completely-missing-SNV guarantee is a pre-filtering ascertainment property of the raw VCF union V. After sample-specific random deletion and reference imputation a low-frequency site can lose all of its remaining derived copies in the imputed haplotypes and be scored monomorphic reference.

Hence in any finite albeit arbitrarily large panel E[Sobs] < E[Strue] and

θ̂W obs = Sobs / a_n

is systematically depressed relative to the true θW on V. Several colleagues already noted this explicitly: E[Sobs] < E[Strue] by the O(1) term -log(1-f), i.e. an O(1/log n) downward finite-sample bias in θW, with the familiar singleton loss. The absolute loss -log(1-f) never vanishes; it is only negligible relative to a_n because a_n diverges slowly.

So the procedure removes variation in two ways: it can erase whole segregating sites when the few carriers are the ones filtered, depressing S and θW, and it attenuates allele frequencies, depressing π. The π bias is a non-vanishing constant-factor bias in the limit, the θW bias is a real systematic downward bias in the site count that underlies θW for the data we compute with. I think the finite-sample interpretation is the one that matters here, and it pushes us toward both estimators being systematically down.

We all agree on the thinning model $Y_{ij}=X_{ij}R_{ij}$ with $R_{ij}\sim Bern(r)$, $r=1-f$, so $E[\hat p|p]=rp$ and 
$\Pr\{K=0|k\}=f^{k}$, $\Pr\{\text{segregating after imputation}|k\}=1-f^{k}$.
Reference imputation can only go derived $\to$ reference, never the reverse.

Nucleotide diversity is the easy case. Conditional on true $p$ 
$E[|Y_1-Y_2||p]=2rp[1-rp]<2p(1-p)$ so $E[\hat\pi_i|p_i]=2rp_i[1-rp_i]<2p_i(1-p_i)$. The thinning $p\to rp$ and the replacement of filtered derived copies by the reference allele deflates heterozygosity by the constant factor $r$ for every $p>0$ and that bias does not vanish with $n$.

Watterson is $0/1$ in principle but the $0/1$ is not preserved after per-sample deletion + reference imputation. On the pre-filtering ascertained union $V$

$E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{s}[1-f^{k_s}]=S_{true}-\sum_s f^{k_s}<S_{true}$

for every realisable panel. Under infinite sites $E[\#sites\;with\;k]\propto 1/k$ so the expected absolute number of segregating sites lost is

$E[S_{true}-S_{obs}]=\sum_{k\ge1} f^{k}/k=-\log(1-f)>0$,

an $O(1)$ loss concentrated on the rare-variant tail that dominates $S$ and $\pi$. Relative to $E[S_{true}]=\theta a_n$, $a_n\sim\log n$, the relative loss is $O(1/\log n)$ and tends to $0$ as $n\to\infty$ for fixed $p$, but the $n\to\infty$ limit is an idealisation.

The “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ guarantee is a pre-filtering ascertainment property of the raw VCF. After sample-specific random deletion the imputed allele at a haplotype is the true derived allele only with probability $r$. A low frequency site with bounded $k$ can lose all of its remaining derived copies in the imputed haplotypes and be called monomorphic reference. As the panel grows the site frequency spectrum keeps feeding in new $k=1,2,\dots$ sites, so there is always a non-vanishing fraction of sites for which $f^{k}$ is not negligible.

Hence for the data we actually compute, i.e. after imputation, we have $E[S_{obs}]<E[S_{true}]$ and 
$\hat\theta_W^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_n$ is systematically depressed relative to the true $\theta_W$ on $V$. The bias is $O(1)$ absolute, $O(1/\log n)$ relative, and is real for any finite albeit arbitrarily large panel. 

In practice we compute both estimators from a downward biased site count and downward biased allele frequencies. Reference imputation therefore deflates both the presence/absence statistic used by Watterson and the frequency-weighted statistic $\pi$, with $\pi$ being more severely and persistently affected. That is the conservative finite-sample picture for the imputed sequences described.
